newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money eases, gilt yields marginally up.
newsitem.headline: India call money eases, gilt yields marginally up.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday around 6.50 percent, down from the day's opening quotes of 9.25-9.75 percent, dealers said.
Call money ended down as banks seemed to have covered their positions, they said.
"We are into the second week of the reporting fortnight," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Call rates tend to ease in the second week."
Dealers also said sentiment had eased after Monday's sale of 13.85 percent ten-year government of India stock failed to attract even 50 percent subscription.
Subscriptions for only 9.68 billion were received against the sale amount of 20 billion rupees, they said.
"Sentiment definitely improved as the market realised the outflow of funds from banks would be less than expected," a dealer at a foreign bank said.

Dealers said yields on government securities (gilts) fell slightly as call money eased. Most of the day's deals were reported in short-dated securities with maturiites up to two years and in treasury bills.
"The softening call rates led to some interest in securities," a dealer said, adding, "buying interest pushed up prices slightly."
Treasury bills maturing in mid-September were traded at yields of 8.75 percent while treasury bills maturing in July 1997 were traded at 12.85 percent, dealers said.
Two-year securities were traded at yields of around 13.55 percent, down from around 13.60 percent on Monday, dealers said.
No trades were reported in commercial paper or certificates of deposit. Dealers said rates on inter-corporate remained steady in the 17-19 percent range for top-rated borrowers.
